note: Literature confirms MAU2 variants present across a spectrum often milder than classic NIPBL CdLS, with overlapping cohesinopathy features that make clinical discrimination from other non-classical CdLS genes challenging without molecular testing.

evidence.text: Individuals with pathogenic variants in MAU2 present with a clinical spectrum ranging from classic CdLS to milder presentations, primarily exhibiting microcephaly and short stature.

source.title: Pathogenic variants in the cohesin loader subunit MAU2 lead to a new Cornelia de Lange Syndrome subtype
source.quote: Affected individuals display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly as consistent features.

evidence.text: Severe CdLS typically features pronounced limb reduction abnormalities such as missing forearms and oligodactyly, whereas milder subtypes across cohesinopathy genes including MAU2, RAD21, and SMC3 show less severe limb and cognitive involvement.

source.title: Cornelia de Lange Syndrome - GeneReviews - NCBI - NIH
source.quote: Severe (classic) CdLS is characterized by distinctive facial features, growth failure (often prenatal onset; height and weight <5th centile throughout life), hypertrichosis, and limb abnormalities (e.g., complete absence of elbow and forearms, oligodactyly [missing digits], micromelia [small hands], subtle phalangeal abnormalities). Individuals with a milder phenotype have less severe growth, cognitive, and limb involvement, but often have facial features consistent with CdLS.
